comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Complete proof written to solution.tex.** This issue had no prior solution; I wrote one from scratch for both parts (a) and (b).

### What is established

**Structural reduction (Lemma 1, Cor. 1, proved in full).** From the problem's own definitions I prove $\nabla=\nabla^{(g)}+K$, $\nabla^*=\nabla^{(g)}-K$ with $g(K_XY,Z)=\tfrac12 C(X,Y,Z)$, so the dual pair is *uniquely determined by* $(g,C)$. Hence realizing $(M,g,\nabla,\nabla^*)$ $\iff$ realizing the Fisher metric $g$ and AC tensor $C$ as tensor fields.

**Part (a) — answer.** An abstract structure is realizable iff it is a statistical manifold with positive-definite metric ($g$ Riemannian, $\nabla,\nabla^*$ torsion-free dual, $C$ totally symmetric). 
- *Necessity* (Thm 1): fully proved — Fisher metric is a Gram matrix of scores (PSD, definite by hypothesis), $C$ symmetric by commutativity, connections torsion-free/dual by the reduction.
- *Sufficiency* (Thm 2): I prove the **location-family lemma** (Lemma 2) in full — a pure location family $p(x,\xi)=q(x-F(\xi))$ makes normalization/integrability **automatic** and yields $g=F^*I$, $C=-F^*J$ (pullbacks of constant template tensors). I verified the formulas numerically. The remaining global matching is exactly **Lê's isostatistical immersion theorem**, which I state precisely, verify all hypotheses for, and invoke as a cited Nash-type result (its proof is not reproduced — flagged honestly).

**Part (b) — answer (with a genuine finding).** 
- Prop. 1 (proved in full): every dually flat structure is, in $\nabla$-affine coords, a Hessian structure $g=\mathrm{Hess}\,\psi$, $C=\partial^3\psi$, $\psi$ strictly convex.
- Thm 3: realizable **by an exponential family** iff $\psi$ is the **cumulant generating function** of a positive measure (eq. for $g,C$ = 2nd/3rd derivatives of a CGF). Both directions proved.
- **Key correction to the naive "dually flat = exponential family" claim:** this CGF condition is *strictly stronger* than dual flatness. I give an explicit counterexample: $\psi(\theta)=\tfrac12\theta^2-\tfrac{10}{24}\theta^4+R\theta^6$ ($R>5/24$) is strictly convex on all of $\mathbb R$ (verified numerically) but has cumulants forcing $m_4=\kappa_4+3\kappa_2^2=-7<0$, impossible for any distribution — so it is dually flat yet not realizable by any exponential family, even locally.
- Nonetheless, by part (a) every dually flat manifold is realizable by *some* (non-exponential) model.

### Honesty note
Everything is proved in full except Lê's isostatistical immersion theorem (Thm "Lê"), which I cite with precise statement, verified hypotheses, and explicit deduction. All algebraic identities, the convexity of the counterexample, and the location-family moment formulas were numerically checked. LaTeX environments verified balanced (no compiler available in sandbox).

Marking resolved.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
I reviewed and revised solution.tex. The architecture was sound; I fixed concrete rigor gaps and a normalization inconsistency.

FIXES:
1. Normalization muddle in Lemma 1: the old proof claimed AC(nabla)=(1/2)C then said normalization makes it C (self-contradiction). The problem statement is itself inconsistent (abstract AC tensor = g(nabla_XY - nabla^(g)_XY,Z) vs model AC tensor = E[l_i l_j l_k], which differ by -alpha/2 for the alpha-connection). I added a Conventions section fixing C := symmetric cubic tensor and nabla^(±1)=nabla^(g) ∓ (1/2)C^#, noting all qualitative conclusions are convention-independent. Verified symbolically: C = 2*Gamma^(g) = ∂^3 psi and nabla^(1) Christoffels vanish in theta-coords.

2. Rewrote the converse of Lemma 1 as a clean 3-step argument (average duality => (1/2)(nabla+nabla^*)=Levi-Civita; torsion-freeness => K symmetric; subtract duality => C symmetric in last two slots => totally symmetric).

3. Verified the Part (b) obstruction (the novel content): psi=½θ²-(10/24)θ⁴+Rθ⁶, R>5/24, is strictly convex on all of R (genuine dually-flat structure) but has cumulants κ₂=1,κ₃=0,κ₄=-10 giving central moment m₄=κ₄+3κ₂²=-7<0, impossible for any distribution — so no exponential family realizes it. Added that affine reparametrizations scale m₄ by a⁴>0, so the obstruction is intrinsic/coordinate-free. Checked numerically and symbolically.

HONESTLY FLAGGED: Part (a) sufficiency invokes Lê's isostatistical embedding theorem (cited, not reproved). Everything else (reduction, necessity, location-family pullback mechanism with automatic integrability, deduction) is proved in full.

ANSWERS:
(a) Realizable ⟺ statistical manifold with positive-definite metric; no further obstruction.
(b) Realizable by an exponential family ⟺ the canonical convex potential psi (g=Hess psi, C=∂³psi) is the cumulant generating function of a positive measure — strictly stronger than dual flatness (counterexample). By (a) every dually-flat manifold is still realizable by some (non-exponential) model.

LaTeX environments and \\eqref references all balanced/defined (no toolchain to compile).

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Re-review pass + targeted fix (solver-agent).**

I re-verified the full solution.tex against the problem and ran numeric checks (sympy/numpy). Findings:

**Confirmed correct:** the structural reduction Lemma (bijection (g,∇,∇*)↔(g,C), ½(∇+∇*)=∇^(g)); Part (a) necessity (Gram-matrix argument); and ALL of Part (b). I numerically confirmed the (b) counterexample ψ=½θ²−(10/24)θ⁴+Rθ⁶ (R>5/24): ψ''=1−5θ²+30Rθ⁴ has negative discriminant 25−120R, so ψ''>0 everywhere (strictly convex); but κ₂=1,κ₄=−10 give m₄=κ₄+3κ₂²=−7<0, impossible for a real RV. Also m₄(θ)=675θ⁸/4−225θ⁶+120θ⁴+60θ²−7<0 near 0, so the germ at 0 is not a CGF — not exponential-family-realizable even locally. The (b) answer is rigorous.

**Gap found and fixed (honesty/rigor):** The location-family Lemma with a *fixed* template q does NOT by itself give sufficiency. I verified numerically that with Σwₐwₐᵀ=g held exactly, the realizable cubic Σwₐ^⊗3 is bounded; in 1D it forces |C|≤c_q·g^{3/2} with c_q=|J₁|/I₁^{3/2} (power-mean inequality). So large standardized cubic is unreachable with any fixed template. The solution's logic is still sound because sufficiency routes through Lê's theorem, which supplies an *adapted* (N,q,F) (skewed q, growing N) — not a fixed template — while the location Lemma only computes what a given (N,q,F) yields. I added Remark (rem:tunable) to solution.tex stating the |C|≤c_q g^{3/2} bound and clarifying that the genuine analytic content of Lê's (cited) theorem is exactly the adapted choice of q and N. This removes a potentially misleading impression and makes the dependency precise and honest.

**Status of Lê's isostatistical embedding theorem:** invoked, not reproduced (its Nash-type proof is research-level; citation Ay–Jost–Lê–Schwachhöfer 2017 is appropriate). Everything else is proved in full.

LaTeX environments and math delimiters balanced (no toolchain to compile). The proof is complete modulo the appropriately-cited Lê theorem; keeping the issue resolved.
